metadata.subject: Operating Systems
metadata.title: Explore Processes
metadata.description: Predict valid process-state transitions caused by scheduler, CPU, and I/O events.

learning_objectives: Explain why a process changes state.
Distinguish Ready, Running, Waiting, and Terminated.
Reject impossible transitions in a single-CPU process model.

mission.title: Follow real process events
mission.description: Predict each next state, then let the executable process model apply the event.

introduction.title: A process changes state as its needs change
introduction.content: A process is a running program. It may wait for CPU time, use the CPU, pause for I/O, or finish.
points: WAITING means paused for an event such as disk I/O.

worked_example.title: One CPU and one I/O request
worked_example.content: The event—not memorized arrow order—determines the next valid state.

steps.explanation: The scheduler gives the available CPU to a ready process.
P1 cannot use the CPU while waiting for the I/O result.
Completion makes P1 eligible for CPU time again.

worked_example.conclusion: A process can only take a transition allowed by its current state and event.

next.title: Now predict it.
next.content: Read each event and choose the state it causes.

action_explanations.predict-running: A scheduler dispatch moves a READY process to RUNNING.
action_explanations.predict-waiting: An I/O request moves a RUNNING process to WAITING.
action_explanations.predict-terminated: A finishing RUNNING process becomes TERMINATED.
action_explanations.predict-ready: I/O completion or a time-slice expiry makes the process READY.

quiz.question: A RUNNING process requests disk I/O. Which state should it enter?

discovery.title: Process-state discovery
discovery.summary: Scheduler, CPU, and I/O events cause valid transitions; a process cannot jump arbitrarily between states.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: A process is a program being managed while it runs or waits.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: RUNNING → WAITING happens when a process requests I/O.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: States tell the operating system which processes can use the CPU and which must wait.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: An event and the current state together determine the only valid transition.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of one service desk
alternate_explanations.content: One customer is being served, others are ready in line, and someone waiting for paperwork cannot use the desk yet.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through P1
alternate_explanations.content: P1 READY → dispatched → RUNNING → asks for disk → WAITING → disk finishes → READY.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does an I/O request move a running process into Waiting?
recall.model_answer: The process cannot continue until the I/O result arrives, so it releases the CPU and waits.
